author: Nadia Farsi
text: This is not a credentials problem. Check /var/log/auth.log - I bet you see 'Disconnected ... [preauth]' mid-authentication.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Yes! Exactly that. What is it?

author: Nadia Farsi
text: Sprinklr's SFTP connector uses an old SSH client that signs RSA keys with the legacy ssh-rsa signature, which is SHA-1. OpenSSH 8.8 and later disabled SHA-1 RSA signatures by default and only accept rsa-sha2-256 or rsa-sha2-512. The server rejects the signature type and drops the connection. The UI surfaces that as a generic connection error, which is why it looks like bad credentials.

author: Nadia Farsi
text:
Quick fix for test, scoped to the sftp group only:
Match Group sftpusers
    PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms +ssh-rsa
then systemctl reload sshd. The rest of the box keeps modern defaults.

author: Nadia Farsi
text: For production do it the other way round - use an ed25519 or ECDSA key for the destination and avoid SHA-1 entirely. Only re-enable ssh-rsa server-side, narrowly scoped, if you have no choice.
